_comment: TEMPORARY DEBUG OVERLAY -- NOT a deployment config. Do not leave this applied.
Purpose: get the main container to actually START on the existing shared pool,
long enough to capture Arweave's own startup logs, WITHOUT repeating the node
eviction. We still have never seen a single line from the arweave-node container.
It does two things:
1. Removes nodeSelector + tolerations, so the pod can land on node4 while the
dedicated pool does not exist yet.
2. Sets memory limit EQUAL to memory request (2560Mi).
This is the safety mechanism. Previously request=2Gi / limit=4Gi made the pod
Burstable: it grew to 3.6 GiB, overran its request by the largest margin of
anything on the node, and the kubelet evicted it -- taking node4 down to 2.2 MiB
free and endangering other teams' pods. Eviction also DELETES the pod, which is
why 'kubectl logs --previous' returned 'not found'.
With limit == request the container is OOMKilled by its own cgroup at 2560Mi.
It can never exceed its request, so its eviction score stays <= 0 and the node
is never starved. The pod object SURVIVES an OOMKill, so --previous logs work.
Expect roughly 40-60 seconds of runtime before the OOMKill -- it reached 2.9 GiB
last time. That is enough to prove: binary executes, config.json parses, the
HTTP listener binds 1984, and the join begins. It is NOT enough to sync.
No CPU limit is set: CPU limits cause CFS throttling and are irrelevant to the
memory eviction we are guarding against.
APPLY:
kubectl patch statefulset arweave-node -n arweave --type=strategic --patch-file DEBUG-patch.json
REVERT (do this as soon as you have the logs):
kubectl apply -f 03-statefulset.yaml
